newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LINKE KEEPS SCHALKE'S UEFA DREAM ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LINKE KEEPS SCHALKE'S UEFA DREAM ALIVE.

text.p: Schalke defender Thomas Linke was the hero up front as well as at the back on Tuesday when his team beat Valencia 2-0 in their UEFA Cup quarter-final first leg.

Schalke were desperate to reach their first European semifinal since 1970 and Linke gave them what they were looking for just before halftime with an unstoppable header from a free-kick from captain Olaf Thon.
"We practiced free-kicks this morning and that worked very well," said Linke. "I don't know whether this will be enough but I think we've managed a very good starting position."
Linke had also hooked away Valencia's most dangerous attack in the first two minutes, when striker Machado Leandro, frustrated by the crossbar moments earlier, pounded a shot on target.
Schalke coach Huub Stevens, who said he would have settled for a 0-0 draw before the game, said hard work had paid off.
"We must be very happy with 2-0 but we've still got another 90 minutes to go and that will be very difficult. But I think we've got a good chance to go further," Stevens said.

Belgian striker Marc Wilmots, who had been doubtful with back problems, wrapped up a disappointing game played in front of a sell-out crowd of 56,824, in the 82nd minute with a tap-in goal from a Jiri Nemec cross.
The bad news for Schalke, though, is that both Wilmots and Linke collected yellow cards and are barred from playing in the return in a fortnight.

Valencia, eleventh in the Spanish first division but missing international keeper Andoni Zubizarreta, Croatian striker Goran Vlaiovic and captain Francisco Camarasa, had dominated the first 20 minutes, but Schalke took the initiative with two good chances in the first half before Linke's goal put them ahead.
